question: Which one of the following limbs of Vedas is known for the explanation and meaning of complex words?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nirukta**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nirukta** is one of the six Vedangas, which are auxiliary disciplines associated with the study and understanding of the Vedas.
 
• The primary function of Nirukta is to provide explanations and meanings of complex and archaic words found in the Vedic texts.
 
• It serves as an important tool for interpreting the Vedic hymns and mantras, thereby facilitating a deeper comprehension of the Vedic literature.
 
• The most famous work on Nirukta is the **Nirukta** of Yaska, an ancient Indian scholar.
 
• Yaska's Nirukta is a lexicon that systematically explains the etymology and meaning of difficult Vedic words.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Vedangas are six auxiliary disciplines developed to support the understanding and practice of the Vedas. These include Shiksha (phonetics), Chhanda (meter), Vyakarana (grammar), Nirukta (etymology), Jyotisha (astronomy and astrology), and Kalpa (ritual).
 
• Each Vedanga plays a crucial role in preserving and interpreting the Vedic texts, ensuring that the knowledge contained within them is accurately transmitted through generations.
 
• Nirukta, in particular, helps scholars and practitioners to decode the ancient language and context of the Vedas, which is essential for accurate ritual performance and philosophical understanding.
 
• The Vedangas are considered essential for anyone engaged in serious Vedic study, as they provide the necessary tools to unlock the deeper meanings and applications of the Vedic hymns.
